sanskrit: hatvā tu taṃ bhīmabalaṃ virādhaṃ rākṣasaṃ vane tataḥ sītāṃ pariṣvajya samāśvāsya ca vīryavān abravīl lakṣmaṇāṃ rāmo bhrātaraṃ dīptatejasaṃ
english: Having slain Virādha, that demon of terrible strength, in the forest, the valiant Rāma then embraced Sītā, comforted her, and spoke to his brother Lakṣmaṇa of blazing splendour.

sanskrit: kaṣṭaṃ vanam idaṃ durgaṃ na ca smo vanagocarāḥ abhigacchāmahe śīghraṃ śarabhaṅgaṃ tapodhanam
english: "This forest is terrible and difficult to traverse, and we are not accustomed to woodland living. Let us quickly go to Śarabhaṅga, that treasury of ascetic merit."

sanskrit: āśramaṃ śarabhaṅgasya rāghavo 'bhijagāma ha
english: And so Rāghava proceeded to the hermitage of Śarabhaṅga.

sanskrit: tasya devaprabhāvasya tapasā bhāvitātmanaḥ samīpe śarabhaṅgasya dadarśa mahad adbhutam
english: Near Śarabhaṅga—that one whose soul had been purified by asceticism and who possessed the radiance of a god—Rāma beheld a great and wondrous sight.

sanskrit: vibhrājamānaṃ vapuṣā sūryavaiśvānaropamam asaṃspṛśantaṃ vasudhāṃ dadarśa vibudheśvaram
english: He saw the lord of the gods, his form blazing like the sun and fire combined, not touching the earth.

sanskrit: suprabhābharaṇaṃ devaṃ virajo 'mbaradhāriṇam tadvidhair eva bahubhiḥ pūjyamānaṃ mahātmabhiḥ
english: The god was adorned with brilliant ornaments, wore spotless garments, and was being venerated by many great-souled beings of his own kind.

sanskrit: haribhir vājibhir yuktam antarikṣagataṃ ratham dadarśādūratas tasya taruṇādityasaṃnibham
english: From a distance Rāma beheld his chariot standing aloft in the sky, yoked with tawny horses, resembling the newly risen sun.

sanskrit: pāṇḍurābhraghanaprakhyaṃ candramaṇḍalasaṃnibham apaśyad vimalaṃ chatraṃ citramālyopaśobhitam
english: He saw a pure white parasol resembling a dense pale cloud or the orb of the moon, adorned with varied garlands.

sanskrit: cāmaravyajane cāgrye rukmadaṇḍe mahādhane gṛhīte vananārībhyāṃ dhūyamāne ca mūrdhani
english: Two foremost fly-whisks of yak-tail hair, fitted with golden handles of great worth, were held by forest women and waved above his head.

sanskrit: gandharvāmarasiddhāś ca bahavaḥ paramarṣayaḥ antarikṣagataṃ devaṃ vāgbhir agryābhir īḍire
english: Many gandharvas, immortals, siddhas, and supreme sages were praising the god stationed in the sky with choice words of hymn.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā śatakratuṃ tatra rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt ye hayāḥ puruhūtasya purā śakrasya naḥ śrutāḥ antarikṣagatā divyās ta ime harayo dhruvam
english: Beholding the Performer of a Hundred Sacrifices there, Rāma said to Lakṣmaṇa: "Those tawny horses moving through the sky—these are certainly the divine horses of Puruhūta, of Śakra, of whom we have heard tell."

sanskrit: ime ca puruṣavyāghra ye tiṣṭhanty abhito ratham śataṃ śataṃ kuṇḍalino yuvānaḥ khaḍgapāṇayaḥ
english: "And these, O tiger among men, who stand around the chariot in hundreds upon hundreds—young, wearing earrings, swords in hand—"

sanskrit: urodeśeṣu sarveṣāṃ hārā jvalanasaṃnibhāḥ rūpaṃ bibhrati saumitre pañcaviṃśativārṣikam
english: "—on each one's chest gleam garlands like flames; they all bear the appearance, O son of Sumitrā, of twenty-five years of age."

sanskrit: etad dhi kila devānāṃ vayo bhavati nityadā yatheme puruṣavyāghrā dṛśyante priyadarśanāḥ
english: "For such, they say, is the eternal age of the gods—just as these tiger-like men appear, so pleasing to behold."

sanskrit: ihaiva saha vaidehyā muhūrtaṃ tiṣṭha lakṣmaṇa yāvaj janāmy ahaṃ vyaktaṃ ka eṣa dyutimān rathe
english: "Stay here a moment with Vaidehī, Lakṣmaṇa, while I find out clearly who this radiant one in the chariot is."

sanskrit: tam evam uktvā saumitrim ihaiva sthīyatām iti abhicakrāma kākutsthaḥ śarabhaṅgāśramaṃ prati
english: Having thus addressed Saumitri with the words "remain right here," Kākutstha advanced toward the hermitage of Śarabhaṅga.

sanskrit: tataḥ samabhigacchantaṃ prekṣya rāmaṃ śacīpatiḥ śarabhaṅgam anujñāpya vibudhān idam abravīt
english: Then the lord of Śacī, seeing Rāma approaching, took leave of Śarabhaṅga and said this to the celestials:

sanskrit: ihopayāty asau rāmo yāvan māṃ nābhibhāṣate niṣṭhāṃ nayata tāvat tu tato māṃ draṣṭum arhati
english: "That Rāma is coming here. Until he has not yet spoken to me, lead on to the conclusion; thereafter he is worthy to behold me."

sanskrit: jitavantaṃ kṛtārthaṃ ca draṣṭāham acirād imam karma hy anena kartavyaṃ mahad anyaiḥ suduṣkaram
english: "I shall behold him ere long as one who has conquered and accomplished his purpose—for a great deed, exceedingly hard for others to perform, is yet to be done by him."

sanskrit: iti vajrī tam āmantrya mānayitvā ca tāpasaṃ rathena hariyuktena yayau divam ariṃdamaḥ
english: Thus speaking, the wielder of the thunderbolt took his leave of the ascetic, paid him honour, and with his chariot yoked to tawny horses, that subduer of foes ascended to the sky.

sanskrit: prayāte tu sahasrākṣe rāghavaḥ saparicchadaḥ agnihotram upāsīnaṃ śarabhaṅgam upāgamat
english: When the Thousand-Eyed one had departed, Rāghava with his companions approached Śarabhaṅga, who was tending his sacred fire.

sanskrit: tasya pādau ca saṃgṛhya rāmaḥ sītā ca lakṣmaṇaḥ niṣedus tadanujñātā labdhavāsā nimantritāḥ
english: Rāma, Sītā, and Lakṣmaṇa clasped his feet; then, having received his invitation and being granted a place to stay, they sat down at his bidding.

sanskrit: tataḥ śakropayānaṃ tu paryapṛcchat sa rāghavaḥ śarabhaṅgaś ca tat sarvaṃ rāghavāya nyavedayat
english: Then Rāghava asked about Śakra's visit, and Śarabhaṅga reported all of it to Rāghava.

sanskrit: mām eṣa varado rāma brahmalokaṃ ninīṣati jitam ugreṇa tapasā duṣprāpam akṛtātmabhiḥ
english: "This granter of boons, O Rāma, wished to convey me to Brahmaloka—won by fierce austerity, hard to reach for those who have not disciplined their souls."

sanskrit: ahaṃ jñātvā naravyāghra vartamānam adūrataḥ brahmalokaṃ na gacchāmi tvām adṛṣṭvā priyātithim
english: "Knowing you, O tiger among men, to be near at hand, I would not go to Brahmaloka without having seen you, my cherished guest."

sanskrit: samāgamya gamiṣyāmi tridivaṃ devasevitam akṣayā naraśārdūla jitā lokā mayā śubhāḥ brāhmyāś ca nākapṛṣṭhyāś ca pratigṛhṇīṣva māmakān
english: "Having met with you, I shall depart to the triple heaven frequented by the gods. Accept from me, O tiger among men, the imperishable, auspicious worlds I have won—both those of Brahmā and those on the back of the firmament."

sanskrit: evam ukto naravyāghraḥ sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ ṛṣiṇā śarabhaṅgena rāghavo vākyam abravīt
english: Thus addressed by the sage Śarabhaṅga, Rāghava, that tiger among men versed in all the scriptures, spoke his reply:

sanskrit: aham evāhariṣyāmi sarvāṃl lokān mahāmune āvāsaṃ tv aham icchāmi pradiṣṭam iha kānane
english: "I myself shall win all the worlds, O great sage. But now I desire a dwelling-place appointed for me here in this forest."

sanskrit: rāghaveṇaivam uktas tu śakratulyabalena vai śarabhaṅgo mahāprājñaḥ punar evābravīd vacaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Rāghava, who was equal in might to Śakra, the greatly wise Śarabhaṅga spoke again:

sanskrit: sutīkṣṇam abhigaccha tvaṃ śucau deśe tapasvinam ramaṇīye vanoddeśe sa te vāsaṃ vidhāsyati
english: "Go to the ascetic Sutīkṣṇa in a pure spot, in a delightful region of the forest; he will arrange a dwelling for you."

sanskrit: eṣa panthā naravyāghra muhūrtaṃ paśya tāta mām yāvaj jahāmi gātrāṇi jīrṇaṃ tvacam ivoragaḥ
english: "This is the path, O tiger among men. Behold me for a moment, dear one, while I shed these limbs as a serpent sheds its worn-out skin."

sanskrit: tato 'gniṃ sa samādhāya hutvā cājyena mantravit śarabhaṅgo mahātejāḥ praviveśa hutāśanam
english: Then, having built up the fire and offered oblations of clarified butter with the proper mantras, the greatly resplendent Śarabhaṅga entered the sacrificial flames.

sanskrit: tasya romāṇi keśāṃś ca dadāhāgnir mahātmanaḥ jīrṇaṃ tvacaṃ tathāsthīni yac ca māṃsaṃ ca śoṇitam
english: The fire consumed the great-souled one's body hair and head hair, then his withered skin, then his bones, his flesh, and his blood.

sanskrit: sa ca pāvakasaṃkāśaḥ kumāraḥ samapadyata utthāyāgnicayāt tasmāc charabhaṅgo vyarocata
english: And he became like fire incarnate, a youth renewed; Śarabhaṅga rose up from that funeral pyre and blazed with light.

sanskrit: sa lokān āhitāgnīnām ṛṣīṇāṃ ca mahātmanām devānāṃ ca vyatikramya brahmalokaṃ vyarohata
english: Transcending the worlds of those who maintain the sacred fires, of the great-souled sages, and of the gods, he ascended to Brahmaloka.

sanskrit: sa puṇyakarmā bhuvane dvijarṣabhaḥ pitāmahaṃ sānucaraṃ dadarśa ha pitāmahaś cāpi samīkṣya taṃ dvijaṃ nananda susvāgatam ity uvāca ha
english: That doer of meritorious deeds, that bull among twice-borns in the world, beheld the Grandfather accompanied by his attendants; and the Grandfather too, beholding that twice-born, rejoiced and said, "Welcome, thou art truly welcome."

sanskrit: śarabhaṅge divaṃ prāpte munisaṃghāḥ samāgatāḥ abhyagacchanta kākutsthaṃ rāmaṃ jvalitatejasaṃ
english: When Śarabhaṅga had attained heaven, assembled throngs of sages came forward to meet Kākutstha Rāma, blazing with splendour.

sanskrit: vaikhānasā vālakhilyāḥ saṃprakṣālā marīcipāḥ aśmakuṭṭāś ca bahavaḥ patrāhārāś ca tāpasāḥ
english: Vaikhānasas, Vālakhilyas, Saṃprakṣālas, Marīcipas, many Aśmakuṭṭas, and ascetics who subsisted on leaves—

sanskrit: dantolūkhalinaś caiva tathaivonmajjakāḥ pare munayaḥ salilāhārā vāyubhakṣās tathāpare
english: —those who used their teeth as mortar, and others who were Unmajjakas; sages who subsisted on water, and others who lived on air—

sanskrit: ākāśanilayāś caiva tathā sthaṇḍilaśāyinaḥ tathordhvavāsino dāntās tathārdrapaṭavāsasaḥ
english: —those who dwelt in the open sky, those who slept on the bare ground, those who stood upright and had mastered their senses, and those who wore constantly wet garments—

sanskrit: sajapāś ca taponityās tathā pañcatapo'nvitāḥ sarve brāhmyā śriyā juṣṭā dṛḍhayogasamāhitāḥ śarabhaṅgāśrame rāmam abhijagmuś ca tāpasāḥ
english: —those ever engaged in muttering sacred syllables, those devoted to austerity, and those who practised the five-fire penance—all endowed with the glory of Brahmā and firmly steadied in yoga: these ascetics from the hermitage of Śarabhaṅga came to Rāma.

sanskrit: abhigamya ca dharmajñā rāmaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ varam ūcuḥ paramadharmajñam ṛṣisaṃghāḥ samāhitāḥ
english: Having approached Rāma, the best among upholders of dharma, the assembled sages, knowing the highest dharma, composed of mind, spoke to him who was supremely learned in dharma:

sanskrit: tvam ikṣvākukulasyāsya pṛthivyāś ca mahārathaḥ pradhānaś cāsi nāthaś ca devānāṃ maghavān iva
english: "You are the great warrior foremost of this Ikṣvāku lineage, and the lord of the earth, as Maghavan is the lord of the gods."

sanskrit: viśrutas triṣu lokeṣu yaśasā vikrameṇa ca pitṛvratatvaṃ satyaṃ ca tvayi dharmaś ca puṣkalaḥ
english: "You are renowned in the three worlds for your glory and your valour; in you abide devotion to a father's vow, truthfulness, and dharma in full bloom."

sanskrit: tvām āsādya mahātmānaṃ dharmajñaṃ dharmavatsalam arthitvān nātha vakṣyāmas tac ca naḥ kṣantum arhasi
english: "Having come to you, O lord, great-souled one, learned in dharma and fond of dharma, we shall speak as suppliants—and may you be pleased to pardon us this."

sanskrit: adhārmas tu mahāṃs tāta bhavet tasya mahīpateḥ yo hared baliṣaḍbhāgaṃ na ca rakṣati putravat
english: "Great adharma would befall that king, dear Rāma, who takes the sixth part of tribute yet does not protect his subjects as a father protects his sons."

sanskrit: yuñjānaḥ svān iva prāṇān prāṇair iṣṭān sutān iva nityayuktaḥ sadā rakṣan sarvān viṣayavāsinaḥ
english: "One who is ever engaged, protecting all dwellers of his realm as his own life-breath, as sons dear as life itself—"

sanskrit: prāpnoti śāśvatīṃ rāma kīrtiṃ sa bahuvārṣikīm brahmaṇaḥ sthānam āsādya tatra cāpi mahīyate
english: "—such a one attains, O Rāma, eternal fame lasting many years; and having reached the realm of Brahmā, he is glorified even there."

sanskrit: yat karoti paraṃ dharmaṃ munir mūlaphalāśanaḥ tatra rājñaś caturbhāgaḥ prajā dharmeṇa rakṣataḥ
english: "Whatever supreme dharma a sage subsisting on roots and fruits performs—a quarter share of that accrues to a king who protects his subjects with righteousness."

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ brāhmaṇabhūyiṣṭho vānaprasthagaṇo mahān tvan nātho 'nāthavad rāma rākṣasair vadhyate bhṛśam
english: "This great assembly of forest-dwellers, composed mostly of brahmins, is being slaughtered grievously by rākṣasas, O Rāma, as though it had no lord, though you are its lord."

sanskrit: ehi paśya śarīrāṇi munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām hatānāṃ rākṣasair ghorair bahūnāṃ bahudhā vane
english: "Come and behold the bodies of the sages, those who had purified their souls, slain in manifold ways throughout the forest by the terrible rākṣasas—so many of them."

sanskrit: pampānadīnivāsānām anumandākinīm api citrakūṭālayānāṃ ca kriyate kadanaṃ mahat
english: "A great carnage is being wrought upon those who dwell by the river Pampā, along the Mandākinī, and upon those who make their home on Citrakūṭa."

sanskrit: evaṃ vayaṃ na mṛṣyāmo viprakāraṃ tapasvinam kriyamāṇaṃ vane ghoraṃ rakṣobhir bhīmakarmabhiḥ
english: "Thus we can no longer endure the terrible injury being done to ascetics in the forest by the rākṣasas of fearful deeds."

sanskrit: tatas tvāṃ śaraṇārthaṃ ca śaraṇyaṃ samupasthitāḥ paripālaya no rāma vadhyamānān niśācaraiḥ
english: "Therefore we have come to you, the refuge-giver, seeking refuge. Protect us, O Rāma—we who are being slain by the night-wanderers."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu kākutsthas tāpasānāṃ tapasvinām idaṃ provāca dharmātmā sarvān eva tapasvinaḥ naivam arhatha māṃ vaktum ājñāpyo 'haṃ tapasvinam
english: Having heard this from the ascetics—those men of tapas—the dharma-souled Kākutstha addressed all the ascetics: "You ought not speak to me in this fashion; I am one who takes orders from ascetics."

sanskrit: bhavatām arthasiddhyartham āgato 'haṃ yadṛcchayā tasya me 'yaṃ vane vāso bhaviṣyati mahāphalaḥ tapasvināṃ raṇe śatrūn hantum icchāmi rākṣasān
english: "I have come here by good fortune precisely to accomplish your purpose; this sojourn of mine in the forest shall bear great fruit. I desire to slay in battle the rākṣasas who are the enemies of the ascetics."

sanskrit: dattvā varaṃ cāpi tapodhanānāṃ dharme dhṛtātmā sahalakṣmaṇena tapodhanaiś cāpi sahārya vṛttaḥ sutīṣkṇam evābhijagāma vīraḥ
english: Having granted a boon to those whose wealth was tapas, the hero, steadfast in dharma, conducted himself nobly with those ascetics; and together with Lakṣmaṇa, accompanied by those ascetics, he proceeded onward to Sutīkṣṇa himself.

sanskrit: rāmas tu sahito bhrātrā sītayā ca paraṃtapaḥ sutīkṣṇasyāśramapadaṃ jagāma saha tair dvijaiḥ
english: Rāma, that scorcher of foes, accompanied by his brother and by Sītā, went to the hermitage of Sutīkṣṇa together with those twice-born sages.

sanskrit: sa gatvā dūram adhvānaṃ nadīs tīrtva bahūdakāḥ dadarśa vipulaṃ śailaṃ mahāmegham ivonnatam
english: Travelling a long way, crossing rivers full of water, he beheld a vast mountain range towering like a great rain cloud.

sanskrit: tatas tad ikṣvākuvarau satataṃ vividhair drumaiḥ kānanaṃ tau viviśatuḥ sītayā saha rāghavau
english: Then those two best of the Ikṣvāku line, the two Rāghavas, entered that forest thick with diverse trees, together with Sītā.

sanskrit: praviṣṭas tu vanaṃ ghoraṃ bahupuṣpaphaladrumam dadarśāśramam ekānte cīramālāpariṣkṛtam
english: Having entered the awesome forest with its many flowering and fruit-bearing trees, he saw in a secluded spot a hermitage adorned with garlands of bark-cloth strips.

sanskrit: tatra tāpasam āsīnaṃ malapaṅkajaṭādharam rāmaḥ sutīkṣṇaṃ vidhivat tapovṛddham abhāṣata
english: There, seated, wearing matted locks caked with mud and grime, great in his asceticism—Rāma duly addressed the ascetic Sutīkṣṇa.

sanskrit: rāmo 'ham asmi bhagavan bhavantaṃ draṣṭum āgataḥ tan mābhivada dharmajña maharṣe satyavikrama
english: "I am Rāma, O Blessed One; I have come to behold you. So speak to me, O knower of dharma, O great sage of true valour."

sanskrit: sa nirīkṣya tato vīraṃ rāmaṃ dharmabhṛtāṃ varam samāśliṣya ca bāhubhyām idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: He then gazed upon Rāma, that hero, the best among upholders of dharma, and embraced him with both arms, saying these words:

sanskrit: svāgataṃ khalu te vīra rāma dharmabhṛtāṃ vara āśramo 'yaṃ tvayākrāntaḥ sanātha iva sāmpratam
english: "Welcome indeed to you, O hero Rāma, best among upholders of dharma! This hermitage, now that you have entered it, is like one that has found a master."

sanskrit: pratīkṣamāṇas tvām eva nārohe 'haṃ mahāyaśaḥ devalokam ito vīra dehaṃ tyaktvā mahītale
english: "Waiting for you alone, O greatly renowned one, I have not ascended to the world of the gods from this place by abandoning my body upon the earth, O hero."

sanskrit: citrakūṭam upādāya rājyabhraṣṭo 'si me śrutaḥ ihopayātaḥ kākutstho devarājaḥ śatakratuḥ sarvāṃl lokāñ jitān āha mama puṇyena karmaṇā
english: "From when you took up residence at Citrakūṭa, having been deprived of your kingdom, I heard of your coming here, O Kākutstha; and Indra, the king of the gods, the Performer of a Hundred Sacrifices, declared that all the worlds had been won by me through my meritorious deeds."

sanskrit: teṣu devarṣijuṣṭeṣu jiteṣu tapasā mayā matprasādāt sabhāryas tvaṃ viharasva salakṣmaṇaḥ
english: "In those worlds frequented by gods and sages, won by me through austerity—by my grace, roam freely together with your wife and with Lakṣmaṇa."

sanskrit: tam ugratapasaṃ dīptaṃ maharṣiṃ satyavādinam pratyuvācātmavān rāmo brahmāṇam iva vāsavaḥ
english: To that blazing great sage of fierce austerity and truthful speech, the self-possessed Rāma replied as Vāsava might reply to Brahmā:

sanskrit: aham evāhariṣyāmi svayaṃ lokān mahāmune āvāsaṃ tv aham icchāmi pradiṣṭam iha kānane
english: "I myself shall win the worlds, O great sage. But I desire a dwelling-place appointed for me here in this forest."

sanskrit: bhavān sarvatra kuśalaḥ sarvabhūtahite rataḥ ākhyātaḥ śarabhaṅgena gautamena mahātmanā
english: "You have been described to me by Śarabhaṅga and by the great-souled Gautama as one skilled in all matters and devoted to the welfare of all beings."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa maharṣir lokaviśrutaḥ abravīn madhuraṃ vākyaṃ harṣeṇa mahatāplutaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Rāma, the great sage, renowned through the worlds, flooded with great joy, spoke sweet words:

sanskrit: ayam evāśramo rāma guṇavān ramyatām iha ṛṣisaṃghānucaritaḥ sadā mūlaphalair yutaḥ
english: "This very hermitage, O Rāma, is endowed with good qualities; take your delight here. Frequented always by assemblies of sages, it abounds in roots and fruits."

sanskrit: imam āśramam āgamya mṛgasaṃghā mahāyaśāḥ aṭitvā pratigacchanti lobhayitvākutobhayāḥ
english: "Herds of deer, O greatly renowned one, come to this hermitage, roam about fearlessly, tempting one to hunt, and depart again."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ tasya maharṣer lakṣmaṇāgrajaḥ uvāca vacanaṃ dhīro vikṛṣya saśaraṃ dhanuḥ
english: Hearing those words of the great sage, the elder brother of Lakṣmaṇa—the steadfast one—spoke, drawing his bow with arrow nocked:

sanskrit: tān ahaṃ sumahābhāga mṛgasaṃghān samāgatān hanyāṃ niśitadhāreṇa śareṇāśanivarcasā
english: "Those deer that come in herds, O greatly fortunate one, I would slay with a sharp-edged arrow blazing like a thunderbolt—"

sanskrit: bhavāṃs tatrābhiṣajyeta kiṃ syāt kṛcchrataraṃ tataḥ etasminn āśrame vāsaṃ ciraṃ tu na samarthaye
english: "—but then you would be implicated in that act, and what could be more troublesome than that? Therefore I do not think a long stay in this hermitage advisable."

sanskrit: tam evam uktvā varadaṃ rāmaḥ saṃdhyām upāgamat anvāsya paścimāṃ saṃdhyāṃ tatra vāsam akalpayat
english: Having spoken thus to that granter of boons, Rāma went to perform the evening rites; and having observed the western twilight, he settled there for the night.

sanskrit: tataḥ śubhaṃ tāpasabhojyam annaṃ svayaṃ sutīkṣṇaḥ puruṣarṣabhābhyām tābhyāṃ susatkṛtya dadau mahātmā saṃdhyānivṛttau rajanīṃ samīkṣya
english: Then the great-souled Sutīkṣṇa himself, having duly honoured those two bulls among men, gave them wholesome food fit for an ascetic, as the twilight ended and night set in.
